name: rotation-saves
note: The boot's save fails (a full card): plays.1.jnl (1-4) is covered by no MARK. The next play rotates; the save runs first and lands (MARK 8). The next boot folds what the log still holds above MARK: 9; none lost.

name: rotation-fails
note: The boot's save fails (a full card): plays.1.jnl (1-4) is covered by no MARK. The next play rotates; the save runs first and fails too. The next boot folds what the log still holds above MARK: 5-9; 1-4 are lost to the stats (5.5's undercount, 4).

name: rotation-twin-saves
note: The boot's save fails (a full card): plays.1.jnl (1-4) is covered by no MARK. The next play rotates over a plays.1.jnl a twin's chain holds (renamed to a twin, not deleted); the save runs first and lands (MARK 8). The next boot folds what the log still holds above MARK: 9; none lost.

name: rotation-twin-fails
note: The boot's save fails (a full card): plays.1.jnl (1-4) is covered by no MARK. The next play rotates over a plays.1.jnl a twin's chain holds (renamed to a twin, not deleted); the save runs first and fails too. The next boot folds what the log still holds above MARK: 5-9; 1-4 are lost to the stats (5.5's undercount, 4).

name: flush-in-time
note: The orderly end's flush writes the ninth play, which rotates over plays.1.jnl (1-4, saved by nothing). 3 s of the budget left: the rotation's save runs first; none lost.

name: flush-late
note: The orderly end's flush writes the ninth play, which rotates over plays.1.jnl (1-4, saved by nothing). 0.5 s left: no save, and 1-4 are lost to the stats (4).

name: second-player
note: A saves 1-3 (stats.bin generation 1) and plays 4. The card goes into B, which folds A's 4, compacts (no base yet, nothing playing) and saves (generation 2), then plays B 1. Back in A (a remount, its session going on), A plays 5: Hs is refused, the card's stats.bin no longer the copy A's session stands on (5.5). A's next boot reads B's stats.bin and folds B 1 and A 5: every slot once.

name: nvs-back
note: A plays 1-4; a sync's ACKS (4); the boot folds, saves and trims the log empty. NVS is then put back to seq 1 (a settings backup): the seq rule takes ACKS's and MARK's 4, so the next play is 5 (not 2, which ACKS acknowledges and MARK covers: never sent, never folded); the next boot folds it.

name: alternating
note: A and B take the card in turns, each boot folding the other's plays, a sync's ACKS between (A 3, B 2) trimming what the saved MARK covers: each slot once.

name: old-firmware
note: A saves 1-3, plays 4-6 (live, unsaved), then a sync's ACKS (6) and a boot of 0.14.0, which trims both files without folding them. The next stats boot finds ACKS above MARK with 4-6 in no file: HEAD's gap 3, MARK 6 (5.8's undercount, counted).

name: partial-hs
note: partial-tail's card: the boot's scan fails a read after plays.jnl's third slot (9-11 folded, 12-14 not): no save; A then plays 15 and Hs is refused (a partial scan: no save this session). The next boot reads it all: 12-15 folded once, saved.

name: first-at-live
note: first-at-a's seven slots, B's folded at A's boot and A's live (an undated Auto DJ play, then a dated shuffle one, of Harbour Lights; an undated Auto DJ play of Tidewater; a skip of North Pier), saved by a rotation's save (the log's cap 4: plays.1.jnl holds A's first, which no save covers). Their rows are first-at-a's but lastOrd: the live plays' round is HEAD.round + 2, the boot's + 1. The next boot folds the last play.

name: partial-rotation
note: partial-open's card (the stats' MARK 4; plays.1.jnl 1-8, its open failed at this boot; plays.jnl 9-11): no save this session. The second play rotates over plays.1.jnl, 5-8 unsaved: no save is asked (a partial scan), and 5-8 are lost to the stats (4).

name: log-deleted
note: A plays 1-4 and saves them (MARK 4, no sync). plays.jnl is then deleted on a PC and NVS put back to seq 1: with no log and no ACKS, the seq rule's MARK keeps the next play at 5 (2 would be under MARK: never folded).

name: new-epoch-live
note: A plays 1-3, then its NVS is erased: the next boot draws a new epoch, and with no ACKS its scan still reads (0.14.0's didn't): 1-3 fold once under the old epoch's MARK row, and the new epoch's 1 under its own at the boot after.

name: update-quiet
note: A saves 1-2 at its boot; a library update with nothing new: the give-back writes nothing, the re-read finds the stats.bin it stood on. A plays 3; the next boot folds it.

name: update-plays
note: A plays 1-2 (live, unsaved); an update: the give-back saves them first (generation 1); 3-4 are written during the update, into the ring, and folded after the re-read (the same copy). A plays 5; a second update saves 3-5 first (generation 2), nothing in the ring. Hs then has nothing new; the next boot folds nothing.

name: update-save-fails
note: A saves 1-2 at its boot, plays 3-4; the update's give-back can't save them (a full card) and gives its blocks back all the same. 5 is written during the update. The re-read finds generation 1, which doesn't hold 3-4: 5 is folded, and every later save this session is refused (Hs too), or MARK would cover 3-4 unfolded. The next boot folds 3-6: none lost.

name: update-behind-rotation
note: A saves 1-2 at its boot (MARK 2), plays 3-4; the update's give-back can't save them (a full card) and gives its blocks back all the same. The re-read finds generation 1, which doesn't hold 3-4: the session is behind its log. A plays 5-9: 9 rotates over plays.1.jnl (1-4), whose 3-4 the card's MARK doesn't cover; the rotation's save is refused (behind) and the rotation goes on, so 3-4 are lost to the stats (2). Held through the update, that save would have landed and lost none. The next boot folds 5-9.

name: update-rotation-saved
note: The boot's save fails (a full card): plays.1.jnl (1-4) is covered by no MARK. An update's give-back saves 1-8 first (MARK 8). 9 is written during the update and rotates over plays.1.jnl: MARK covers it, so no save is asked; 9 is folded after the re-read, and the next boot folds it again from the log (nothing saved since). None lost.

name: update-rotation-unsaved
note: The boot's save fails (a full card): plays.1.jnl (1-4) is covered by no MARK. An update's give-back saves 1-8 first and fails too. 9 is written during the update and rotates over plays.1.jnl: its save is refused (the blocks given back), the rotation goes on, and 1-4 are lost to the stats (5.5's hole, 4); the re-read finds no stats.bin, the session is behind its log, and the next boot folds 5-9.

name: update-other-player
note: A saves 1-2, plays 3; an update's give-back saves 3 (generation 2); A 4 is written during it. The card goes into B, which folds A 4, compacts and saves (generation 3), then plays B 1. Back in A (a remount), the re-read finds B's stats.bin: A 4 is in it (MARK covers it: not folded again), but it isn't the copy A stood on, so A's saves are refused for the session (Hs too). A's next boot folds B 1 and A 5: every slot once.

name: update-ending
note: A plays 1-8 (live; plays.1.jnl 1-4 covered by no MARK); an update's give-back saves them first (MARK 8). The orderly end comes before the re-read: its flush writes 9, which rotates over plays.1.jnl, covered by MARK (no save asked); 9 stays in the ring, never folded this session. The next boot folds it: none lost.

name: update-ring-full
note: A plays 1; an update's give-back saves it. 34 plays are written during the update: the ring holds 32, folded after the re-read; 2 go past it, so the session is behind its log and its saves are refused (Hs too). The next boot folds 2-35: none lost.
